arxiv-1610-00429.title: Determining the torus covering factors for a sample of type 1 AGN in the local Universe
arxiv-1610-00429.creator: Savithri H. Ezhikode, Poshak Gandhi, Chris Done, Martin Ward, Gulab C. Dewangan, Ranjeev Misra, Ninan Sajeeth Philip
arxiv-1610-00429.description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Savithri H. Ezhikode, Poshak Gandhi, Chris Done, Martin Ward, Gulab C. Dewangan, Ranjeev Misra, Ninan Sajeeth Philip. In the unified scheme of active galactic nuclei, a dusty torus absorbs and then reprocesses a fraction of the intrinsic luminosity which is emitted at longer wavelengths.

arxiv-2312-06612.title: Scalar fields in Bonnor-Melvin-Lambda universe with potential: A study of dynamics of spin-zero particles-antiparticles
arxiv-2312-06612.description: Abstract In this study, our primary focus is on exploring the relativistic quantum dynamics of spin-zero scalar particles in a magnetic space-time background. Our investigation revolves around solving the Klein-Gordon (KG) equation within the framework of an electrovacuum space-time, while incorporating an external scalar potential.

arxiv-2401-11066.title: Formation and Study of a Spherical Plasma Liner for Plasma-Jet-Driven Magneto-Inertial Fusion
arxiv-2401-11066.creator: A. L. LaJoie, F. Chu, A. Brown, S. Langendorf, J. P. Dunn, G. A. Wurden, F. D. Witherspoon, A. Case, M. Luna, J. Cassibry, A. Vyas, M. Gilmore
arxiv-2401-11066.description: Abstract Plasma-jet-driven magneto-inertial fusion (PJMIF) is an alternative approach to controlled nuclear fusion which aims to utilize a line-replaceable dense plasma liner as a repetitive spherical compression driver. In this experiment, first measurements of the formation of a spherical Argon plasma liner formed from 36 discrete pulsed plasma jets are obtained on the Plasma Liner Experiment (PLX).

arxiv-2504-08198.title: The More is not the Merrier: Investigating the Effect of Client Size on Federated Learning
arxiv-2504-08198.creator: Eleanor Wallach, Sage Siler, Jing Deng
arxiv-2504-08198.description: Abstract Federated Learning (FL) has been introduced as a way to keep data local to clients while training a shared machine learning model, as clients train on their local data and send trained models to a central aggregator. It is expected that FL will have a huge implication on Mobile Edge Computing, the Internet of Things, and Cross-Silo FL.

arxiv-2602-08869.title: A cavity-mediated reconfigurable coupling scheme for superconducting qubits
arxiv-2602-08869.creator: Shinyoung Hwang, Sangyeon Lee, Eunjong Kim
arxiv-2602-08869.description: Abstract Superconducting qubits have achieved remarkable progress in gate fidelity and coherence, yet their typical nearest-neighbor connectivity presents constraints for implementing complex quantum circuits. Here, we introduce a cavity-mediated coupling architecture in which a shared cavity mode, accessed through tunable qubit–cavity couplers, enables dynamically reconfigurable interactions between non-adjacent qubits.

pmc-10564402.title: Prolonged antibiotic prophylaxis after pancreatoduodenectomy: systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-10564402.creator: Daphne H M Droogh, Jesse V Groen, Mark G J de Boer, Joffrey van Prehn, Hein Putter, Bert A Bonsing, Casper H J van Eijck, Alexander L Vahrmeijer, Hjalmar C van Santvoort, Bas Groot Koerkamp, J Sven D Mieog
pmc-10564402.description: BackgroundPrevious studies have reported conflicting results of prolonged antibiotic prophylaxis on infectious complications after pancreatoduodenectomy. This study evaluated the effect of prolonged antibiotics on surgical-site infections (SSIs) after pancreatoduodenectomy.MethodsA systematic review and meta-analysis was undertaken of SSIs in patients with perioperative (within 24 h) versus prolonged antibiotic (over 24 h) prophylaxis after pancreatoduodenectomy.

pmc-11426158.title: Defining the mode of action of cisplatin combined with NUC-1031, a phosphoramidate modification of gemcitabine
pmc-11426158.creator: Dillum Patel, Alison L. Dickson, Greice M. Zickuhr, In Hwa Um, Oliver J. Read, Clarissa M. Czekster, Peter Mullen, David J. Harrison, Jennifer Bré
pmc-11426158.description: Highlights•In this study, we determined that NUC-1031 is a potent DNA damaging agent in biliary tract and ovarian cancer.•NUC-1031 is converted to the active metabolite dFdCTP, which is incorporated into DNA over a prolonged timeframe.•This leads to a cell cycle arrest and DNA damage.

pmc-11453503.title: 7433 Distribution of Kisspeptin Neurons in the Adult Sheep Amygdala
pmc-11453503.creator: A Igler, R Amodei, C E Roselli
pmc-11453503.description: Disclosure: A. Igler: None. R. Amodei: None. C.E. Roselli: None.Kisspeptin (Kiss1) neurons are primarily recognized for their role in regulating reproductive function by stimulating the release of hormones that control puberty and fertility. While these neurons are more commonly associated with the hypothalamus, recent research has suggested their presence in other brain regions, including the amygdala.

pmc-12563557.title: In vitro Comparison of Soft-Tissue Grafting Materials for Periodontal Surgery: A Systematic Review
pmc-12563557.creator: Ojas Anand Gajbhiye, Meghna Chauhan, Mohanasaranya Sethu Muniyasamy, Debarghya Pal, Shanvi Ray, Manish Rathi
pmc-12563557.description: This systematic review was done to examine in vitro research that evaluates the features of different soft tissue grafting materials in periodontal surgery. The search was conducted using the terms “soft tissue grafts,” “periodontal surgery,” “efficacy,” “growth factor,” and “cell viability”.

pmc-12630079.title: The Influence of Hydrogeomorphology on Food Webs in Riverine Landscapes
pmc-12630079.creator: Martin C Thoms, Michael D Delong
pmc-12630079.description: A central tenet of river science is the interaction between flow and the physical habitat template—hydrogeomorphology—that governs biophysical structure and function. While studies have shown how this interplay shapes structural river ecosystem attributes, our knowledge of their influence on ecosystem function is limited.

pmc-12636802.title: Enchondroma of Hands: A Surgical Dilemma and Our Experience
pmc-12636802.creator: Gourab Biswas, Ahmer Zafar, Mrudul Kyada
pmc-12636802.description: Introduction:Enchondroma is the most common benign cartilaginous tumor of the small tubular bones of the hand. Although typically indolent, it may present with pain, swelling, or pathological fracture, and requires careful differentiation from low-grade chondrosarcoma. Management strategies range from observation in asymptomatic cases to surgical curettage with or without grafting in symptomatic lesions.

pmc-12774331.title: Evaluation of Atmospheric Preprocessing Methods and Chlorophyll Algorithms for Sentinel-2 Imagery in Coastal Waters
pmc-12774331.creator: Tori Wolters, Naomi E Detenbeck, Steven Rego, Matthew Freeman
pmc-12774331.description: Cyanobacterial blooms have been increasingly detected in estuaries and freshwater tidal rivers. To enhance detailed monitoring, an efficient approach to detecting algal blooms through remote sensing is needed to focus more detailed monitoring focused on cyanobacteria. In this study, we compared different remote sensing processing methods to determine an efficient approach to mapping chlorophyll-a.

pmc-13094575.title: Prostate Cancer Screening in Somalia: A Perspective on Addressing a Critical Gap in Early Detection
pmc-13094575.creator: Mohamed Serar Yusuf, Rahmo Mohamed Ali
pmc-13094575.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Prostate cancer is one of the leading cancers affecting men worldwide, with a growing burden in sub-Saharan Africa where mortality-to-incidence ratios remain among the highest globally. In many countries within the region, a substantial proportion of patients present with advanced-stage disease, reflecting limited access to early detection and diagnostic services, and despite the demonstrated benefits of screening, these gains have not been equitably realized in low-resource settings.

pmc-13175890.title: Genetic association and machine learning improve the prediction of type 1 diabetes risk
pmc-13175890.creator: Carolyn McGrail, Timothy J Sears, Emily N Griffin, Alexandra L Ghaben, Patrick Smadbeck, Jason Flannick, Parul Kudtarkar, Hannah Carter, Kyle Gaulton
pmc-13175890.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Type 1 diabetes (T1D) has a large genetic component, and expanded genetic studies of T1D can enhance biological and therapeutic discovery and improve risk prediction. Here we performed genome-wide genetic association and fine-mapping analyses in 20,355 T1D and 797,363 nondiabetic individuals of European ancestry and in 10,107 T1D and 19,639 nondiabetic individuals at the MHC locus, which identified 160 risk signals.

pmc-13232731.title: Chemotherapy-induced reactive myelopoiesis promotes expansion of immunosuppressive neutrophil-like monocytes in mice and humans
pmc-13232731.creator: Huidong Shi, Zhi-Chun Ding, Ogacheko D Okoko, Xin Wang, George Zhou, Yan Ye, Md Yeashin Gazi, Caitlin Brandle, Lirong Pei, Rafal Pacholczyk, Catherine C Hedrick, Locke J Bryan, Gang Zhou
pmc-13232731.description: Cytotoxic chemotherapy primarily targets rapidly proliferating cancer cells but also depletes normal myeloid cells. The resulting cell loss triggers reactive myelopoiesis, a compensatory process in which hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells in the bone marrow (BM) regenerate myeloid lineages. We previously showed that the alkylating agent cyclophosphamide (CTX) induces myelopoiesis, leading to the expansion of immunosuppressive monocytes in mice.

pmc-13236494.title: The toxic effects of α-hemolysin and β-hemolysin produced by Staphylococcus aureus
pmc-13236494.creator: Qiuyu Zhang, Yu Wu, Dan Luo, Fengshan Fang
pmc-13236494.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) is a Gram-positive bacterium widely distributed in nature, which can cause skin and soft tissue infections, sepsis, pneumonia and other invasive diseases. In recent years, the emergence and spread of drug-resistant strains such as Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Vancomycin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (VRSA) have greatly increased the difficulty of clinical treatment, and there is currently no effective vaccine for the treatment of S. pmc-13352428.title: A systematic review and network meta analysis of first-line immunotherapy for advanced urothelial carcinoma
pmc-13352428.creator: Yang Liu, Yuxuan Song, Jilin Wu, Jincong Li, Wenbo Yang, Yiqing Du, Caipeng Qin, Tao Xu
pmc-13352428.description: Aim: To compare the efficacy and safety of first-line systemic therapies for advanced urothelial carcinoma (UC) and identify the relative benefit–risk profiles of available regimens. Methods: We conducted a systematic review and Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials evaluating first-line systemic therapies for advanced UC (INPLASY2025100112).

pmc-13459460.title: Use of optiflow THRIVE high-flow nasal oxygen system versus a non-rebreather oxygen delivery device in patients with increased risk of airway obstruction in interventional radiology procedures: a randomized pilot study
pmc-13459460.creator: Gang Zheng, Mike Hernandez, Carin A. Hagberg
pmc-13459460.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThe configuration of interventional radiology (IR) suites often limits simultaneous access to the patient’s airway and anesthesia equipment. This constraint may lead to suboptimal sedation in patients at increased risk of airway obstruction due to patient safety concerns.
